unit.title: The passive voice
unit.subtitle: ser vs se vs estar + participle — action, impersonal, and state

grammar.title: Three ways to leave the doer out
grammar.intro: How do you say something was done without dwelling on who did it? Spanish gives you three tools, and they mean different things. The formal ser + participle reports an action (and its participle must agree). The everyday se makes it impersonal. And estar + participle describes the resulting state, not the action. Mixing up ser and estar here changes the meaning entirely.

sections.heading: True passive: ser + past participle (+ por)
sections.body: The formal written passive uses ser + the past participle. The participle behaves like an adjective and agrees in gender and number with the subject. The doer, if named, follows por.

ex.en: The novel was written by Cervantes.

sections.heading: Passive / impersonal se: the everyday choice
sections.body: In speech, Spanish prefers se + a verb that agrees with the thing. It's shorter and far more natural than ser + participle. Use it when the doer doesn't matter.

sections.heading: Estar + participle: the resulting STATE
sections.body: This is the key contrast. Ser + participle = the action happened. Estar + participle = the state that resulted, how things are now. A door doesn't do anything in está cerrada — it's simply closed.

ex.es: La puerta fue cerrada por el guardia.
ex.en: The door was closed by the guard.

takeaways: ser + participle = the action, and the participle agrees: la novela fue escrita, los edificios fueron construidos.
Name the doer with por: fue escrita por Cervantes.
In everyday Spanish, prefer se: se construyeron los edificios, aquí se habla español.
estar + participle = the resulting state now (está cerrada), not the action (fue cerrada).

mistakes.w: La puerta fue cerrada. (meaning: it's closed now)
mistakes.why: For the state now, use estar. Ser + participle reports the action of closing it.

mistakes.w: La novela fue escrito por Cervantes.
mistakes.r: La novela fue escrita por Cervantes.
mistakes.why: The participle agrees with novela (feminine) → escrita, not escrito.
Ser must also agree in number: plural subject → fueron.

exercises.prompt_en: The novel was written by Cervantes.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! Novela es femenina singular → fue escrita.
exercises.no: The participle agrees with novela (feminine singular): “fue escrita”.

exercises.prompt_en: You can't go in: the shop is closed.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Es el estado ahora → estar: está cerrada.
exercises.no: For the state right now, use estar: “está cerrada”.
Plural subject → “Los edificios fueron construidos en 1990”.

exercises.prompt: En este barrio ___ muchos pisos. (venderse, plural)
exercises.prompt_en: In this neighbourhood many flats are sold.
exercises.hint: passive se, plural noun (pisos) → plural verb

exercises.prompt: Match each Spanish form to its meaning.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! You've told action, state and se apart.

exercises.tts: La casa fue vendida por una familia.
accepted: la casa fue vendida por una familia
exercises.translation: The house was sold by a family.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “La casa fue vendida por una familia.”
exercises.no: It was: “La casa fue vendida por una familia.” (The house was sold by a family.)

exercises.scenario: Explaining why you couldn't get in 🏬

lines.speaker: Rosa
lines.en: Why didn't you buy the bread?

exercises.no: You're describing the state it was in → estar: “ya estaba cerrada”.

exercises.en: The novel was written by Cervantes
